The Digital Health Platform Challenge

The problem was not one broken feature. It was the amount of repeated work around delivering care. Each new client meant appointments to coordinate. Each new coaching program could mean rebuilding the same structure again. Practitioners had to keep conversations organized and follow ongoing activity while still focusing on counseling and coaching. As the number of users and programs increased, those small administrative tasks started adding up.

Not Another Standalone Tool

Online counseling and health coaching involve much more than booking an appointment. Practitioners need to manage schedules, communicate with clients, prepare coaching programs, follow ongoing activity, and keep each care journey organized. When those tasks are handled through separate processes, administration starts taking time away from care. The answer was not another standalone tool. Person Care needed the main care workflows to work together.

The Digital Health Platform

DigiWorks AI developed one digital health platform for appointment management, private communication, structured coaching programs, and workflow visibility. Person Care needed one platform that could bring those workflows together and make growth easier to manage, without making the experience more complicated for practitioners or clients.

01

Appointment Management

Clients and practitioners needed a simpler way to manage appointments without relying on repeated manual coordination. A structured booking workflow brought more of that process into one place. This reduced the time spent arranging and managing appointments by approximately 30–40%.

02

Private Client Communication

Care does not stop when a scheduled session ends. Person Care provided a dedicated environment for communication between clients and practitioners. Keeping communication inside the platform made ongoing client activity easier to manage instead of spreading conversations across disconnected channels.

03

Structured Coaching Programs

Each new coaching program could mean rebuilding similar plans and structures by hand. Reusable coaching program templates reduced that repetition. A process that could take close to one working day could instead be completed in roughly 2–3 hours.

04

Clearer Workflow Visibility

As more appointments, clients, and programs became active, practitioners needed a clearer picture of what required attention. Dashboards brought key activity into one place. That visibility helped teams manage more active workflows without increasing administrative work at the same rate.

What DigiWorks AI Custom Built

Each technology had a clear role. React.js supported the user-facing platform. Ruby on Rails handled the core workflows. AWS provided the cloud foundation. The stack was not the story by itself. Its value came from supporting a platform that could handle more activity without making everyday workflows harder to manage. For a broader build, custom software development services can shape a platform around a real care workflow.

Appointment managementPrivate client communicationStructured coaching programsReusable program templatesWorkflow dashboardsPractitioner onboardingClient follow-upReact.js frontendRuby on Rails backendAWS cloud infrastructure

React.js Frontend

React.js supported the user-facing platform and responsive workflows for appointments, dashboards, and ongoing interaction.

Ruby on Rails Backend

Ruby on Rails handled the backend logic behind booking, coaching programs, user workflows, and core application operations.

AWS Cloud Infrastructure

AWS provided the cloud foundation needed to support increasing platform activity and continued product growth.

Why Person Care Could Support 3x More Workflows

  • The increase in capacity did not come from asking practitioners to work faster.
  • It came from reducing repeated work around care delivery.
  • Booking became more structured, and program templates reduced repeated setup.
  • Communication stayed inside the platform, and dashboards made ongoing activity easier to follow.
  • Teams could manage up to 3x more active workflows without the same 3x increase in coordination and administrative effort.

Why This Project Worked

Person Care did not try to solve every healthcare technology problem. It focused on the work practitioners had to repeat every day. Instead of adding more technology around care, the platform reduced the amount of technology practitioners had to think about.

Easier Appointments

Appointments became easier to coordinate. Booking became more structured, so less of that work stayed manual.

Faster Programs

Programs became faster to prepare. Reusable templates cut setup from around one working day to roughly 2–3 hours.

Organized Communication

Client communication stayed organized, and ongoing workflows became easier to see from one place.

A Practical Approach to AI

AI should not be added just because it is available. Person Care’s immediate problem was workflow management, not machine learning. The right first step was building a stable digital health platform around real practitioner and client needs. If future features genuinely require machine learning, MLOps can support reliable deployment, monitoring, and operation at that stage. The technology should follow a real use case, not be forced into the product simply to claim an AI feature.
